query: Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets provide 16 candidate alloys, nine of which are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing. Early reports associated increasing constituent count with greater strength, but that simple relationship is no longer generally accepted. Despite extensive experimental and theoretical investigation, the origins of differences in deformation and failure behavior remain unresolved; practical interpretation must also account for constituent cost and overall cost-performance balance. What testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs these mechanical-property differences and why? Define a controlled investigation, the observations predicted relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline, the limits within which the hypothesis should apply, the prior evidence supporting it, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-based alloys, the variation in mechanical properties among the equiatomic quinary, quaternary, and ternary subsets is primarily governed by differences in lattice distortion. Higher lattice distortion in the full quinary alloy leads to wavy dislocation cores that impede dislocation glide, resulting in higher yield strength and lower ductility compared to versions with fewer constituents, which have reduced lattice distortion.
generation.material_initial_state: Thermomechanically processed single‐phase FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its corresponding quaternary and ternary subsets.
generation.intervention: Synthesize and process reduced-constituent (quaternary and ternary) variants by selectively omitting one or more elements while maintaining a single-phase FCC microstructure.
generation.conditions: All alloys are produced under identical thermomechanical processing conditions (e.g., heat treatment, deformation at room temperature) to ensure comparable grain size and phase purity.
generation.structural_mediator: The degree of lattice distortion, quantified by measuring lattice parameter heterogeneity (via XRD peak broadening) and local strain fields/dislocation core structures (via TEM).
generation.mechanism: Variations in constituent count change the degree of atomic size mismatch (lattice distortion). In the quinary alloy, severe lattice distortion leads to deviations of dislocation cores from their glide planes (wavy dislocation lines), resisting dislocation motion and enhancing yield strength at the expense of ductility. Lower distortion in quaternary/ternary subsets permits easier dislocation glide, reducing strength but improving ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline, quaternary and ternary alloys are predicted to display lower yield strength and higher ductility, concomitant with measurable reductions in lattice distortion indicators.
generation.baseline: Equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy processed under standardized thermomechanical conditions at room temperature.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is expected to hold for single-phase FCC HEAs processed under similar regimes. It may not apply when secondary phases emerge or when processing conditions introduce other confounding microstructural features.
generation.uncertainty: The quantitative correlation between constituent count, lattice distortion, and mechanical properties is not fully defined, and the interplay with microstructural factors (e.g., grain size, residual stresses) introduces additional uncertainty.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of alloys spanning the equiatomic quinary, selected quaternary, and ternary compositions ensuring single-phase FCC microstructures via identical thermomechanical processing. Quantify lattice distortion using XRD and TEM, and perform room-temperature tensile tests to determine yield strength and ductility.
measurements: XRD peak broadening and lattice parameter distribution to assess lattice distortion
Tensile yield strength and elongation-to-fracture measurements
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If measured lattice distortion does not decrease with reduced constituent count or if the mechanical properties (i.e., yield strength and ductility) do not correlate with the distortion level (i.e., quaternary/ternary alloys do not exhibit lower strength and higher ductility than the quinary baseline), then the hypothesis is falsified.

System: Nb23.8Ta25.5Ti24.9V25.8 (nominally Nb25Ta25Ti25V25) BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
